1. Weather passes through

Air temperature in the output matches the met file to within 0.00 °C at every hour, so the model reads the weather as intended.

2. Incoming sunlight on open ground

On open, sunlit ground (sky view above 0.9) the model's incoming shortwave should be close to the weather file's global radiation on a flat surface.

3. Shadows vs an independent ray cast

For each hour I traced rays toward the sun (my own solar-position formula) over the same buildings and trees and marked a ground pixel shaded if anything blocks it, including its own tree. SOLWEIG's own shadow uses its sun position, a slightly different hour convention, and lets 3% of sun through leaves, so small differences are expected. Edge pixels within 150 m of the scene border are skipped.

5. Mean radiant temperature in sun and shade

Expected physics: around midday, Tmrt in shade sits a few degrees above air temperature (warm walls and ground) and in sun it is 20–35 °C higher; early and late, shaded Tmrt drops below air temperature because a clear sky radiates little heat back. The gap follows the sun.
